about: The books of Tom Gally's list "Japan As They Saw It" (JATSI), which are being added to the travel-books project gradually (notes/jatsi.md; Tom, 2026-11-20). Taken on 2026-11-20 from the Sources page of that project. This file is the list itself and does not change when a book is queued or published: a book's state is its row in data/queue.json ("from": "jatsi", "jatsi": n).

fields.n: number in the order of the JATSI page (by year, then as listed)
fields.year: as given on the JATSI page: the year of the copy listed, not always of the first edition
fields.note: JATSI's own remark on the edition or the book
fields.kind: this project's sorting, from JATSI's one-line summary only, 2026-11-20: narrative = a first-person account of the author's own travel or residence; mixed = first-person matter together with much history, survey or essay; other = compilation, history, survey, guidebook, reference work, pamphlet, picture book, translation, fiction. To be corrected when a book is looked at.
fields.summary: JATSI's one-line summary, written by Claude for that project in September 2026 from IA's text and scans; not checked. Not shown on the site.
fields.excerpted_in_jatsi: true if JATSI has passages from the book
fields.scans: the Internet Archive items JATSI links to; images, contributor, date and page_images (a page-image archive exists) from IA's metadata on 2026-11-20. A better scan may exist: look before starting.
fields.sections: JATSI's links to the part of a book that is about Japan
fields.gutenberg: Project Gutenberg ebook numbers: from JATSI's own links and from a title-and-surname match against pg_catalog.csv on 2026-11-20 (no match is not proof that there is no text)
fields.vetted: what a vetting found for a book that was looked at and not queued (so that it is not done twice); queued books have it on their queue row
fields.died_after_1955: an author or contributor known to have died after 1955: no bar for a JATSI book (Tom, 2026-11-20), but the book's notes_on_text must say so (notes/jatsi.md)

books.title: A Visit to India, China, and Japan in the Year 1853
books.author: Bayard Taylor
books.summary: A travel writer’s narrative of a year’s journey through India and China, then, as an acting master’s-mate in Perry’s squadron, to Loo-Choo [Ryukyu], the Bonins [Ogasawara Islands], and the delivery of the President’s letter in July 1853, with the Japan portion admittedly thin

books.title: Hildreth’s Japan As It Was and Is
books.author: Richard Hildreth
books.note: Alternate title: Japan and the Japanese
books.summary: A two-volume compilation by an American historian who never went there, letting successive visitors from the Jesuits through Kämpfer [Kaempfer] and Golownin [Golovnin] to Perry and Townsend Harris speak in their own words, here as edited with supplementary notes by Ernest W. Clement in 1906

books.title: Japan and Around the World
books.author: J. W. Spalding
books.summary: A first-person voyage narrative of the Perry expedition by a commander’s clerk, covering the outward passage, Loo-Choo [Ryukyu], and three visits to Japan in 1853–1854, including the Kanagawa treaty, Simoda [Shimoda], and Hakodadi [Hakodate], with sharp words for the commodore

books.title: Japan: An Account, Geographical and Historical, from the Earliest Period at Which the Islands Composing This Empire Were Known to Europeans, Down to the Present Time, and the Expedition Fitted Out in the United States, etc.
books.author: Charles MacFarlane
books.summary: A compilation made in England from earlier writers, Kämpfer [Kaempfer] above all and Thunberg after him, arranged in eleven books on European intercourse from 1542 to 1849, geography, religion, government, natural products, manners, and language, with the American expedition anticipated rather than narrated

books.title: Narrative of the Expedition of an American Squadron to the China Seas and Japan: Performed in the Years 1852, 1853 and 1854, under the Command of Commodore M.C. Perry
books.author: Matthew C. Perry and Francis L. Hawks
books.summary: The official report of Perry’s expedition, compiled from the Commodore’s journal and officers’ papers, prefaced by a survey of earlier foreign attempts on Japan and covering Lew Chew [Ryukyu], the bay of Yedo [Edo], the Kanagawa treaty of 1854, Simoda [Shimoda], and Hakodadi [Hakodate]

books.title: Notes on the Late Expedition Against the Russian Settlements in Eastern Siberia, and of a Visit to Japan and to the Shores of Tartary, and of the Sea of Okhostk
books.author: Paul Bernard Whittingham
books.summary: A Royal Engineers officer’s notes as a passenger on a British squadron’s 1855 cruise against the Russians, nearly half on Japan, with two stays at Hakodadi [Hakodate], calls at Simoda [Shimoda] and Nagasaki, and a candid verdict on an ill-directed expedition

books.title: My Last Cruise
books.author: A. W. Habersham
books.summary: A lieutenant’s narrative of the North Pacific Surveying and Exploring Expedition of 1853–1855, with Si-mo-da [Shimoda] and a thousand miles of Japanese coast surveyed up to Jesso [Hokkaido], still more pages on Kamtschatka [Kamchatka] and the Okotsk Sea [Sea of Okhotsk], and an extended account of the Ainu

books.title: The Americans in Japan: An Abridgement of the Government Narrative of the U.S. Expedition to Japan, under Commodore Perry
books.author: Robert Tomes
books.summary: A one-volume condensation of the official account of Perry’s expedition, from the outward passage through Lew Chew [Ryukyu] and the Bonins [Ogasawara Islands] to the President’s letter in 1853, the treaty at Yokuhama [Yokohama] in 1854, and the new ports of Simoda [Shimoda] and Hakodadi [Hakodate]

books.title: Japan Opened
books.author: Religious Tract Society
books.summary: A cheap, anonymous English abridgment of the official American narrative of Perry’s expedition, cut down to its Japanese portions and prefixed with a sketch of earlier foreign dealings, with the tract society’s religious argument recurring every fifteen or twenty pages

books.title: Japan and Her People
books.author: Andrew Steinmetz
books.summary: A barrister’s compilation assembled after the British treaty of 1858 from earlier books, MacFarlane among them, covering geography, government, houses, religion, festivals, language, and history, with a composite journey from Nagasaki to Jeddo [Edo], borrowed from Kampfer [Kaempfer], Thunberg, and others and an introduction urging Japanese emigration

books.title: Personal Narrative of a Voyage to Japan, Kamtschatka, Siberia, Tartary, and Various Parts of Coast of China
books.author: J. M. Tronson
books.summary: A naval officer’s narrative from running notes of three seasons on the East India and China station, 1854–1856, opening with Stirling’s squadron at Nagasaki and the Convention of 1854, then pirate-hunting, Kamtschatka [Kamchatka], and the Tartary coast, and a base year at Hakodadi [Hakodate]

books.title: Two Journeys to Japan, 1856-7
books.author: Kinahan Cornwallis
books.summary: A civilian passenger’s two-volume first-person narrative of visits aboard American warships to Simoda [Shimoda], Hakodadi [Hakodate], and Jesso [Hokkaido] in 1856 and to Lew-Kew [Ryukyu] and Nagasaki in 1857, broken by a block of compiled chapters on Japanese history and religion, and closing on the Pacific island of Nookoora

vetted.result: Cornwallis, Two Journeys to Japan (2 vols): only Google scans on IA; the University of California pair (twojourneystoja03corngoog, twojourneystoja02corngoog) is near-bilevel, text legible, but the tinted lithograph plates are washed out or perhaps missing (vol. I frontispiece, plate at p. 24); the Michigan pair seems to lack plates. Rule 3 not met: Ganesha 'Japan in English' (2002) and Elibron (2001). Kinahan Cornwallis 1839–1917. Not queued: lower priority (reprinted, two volumes), and the plates need a better scan.

books.title: Narrative of the Earl of Elgin’s Mission to China and Japan in the Years 1857, ’58, ’59
books.author: Laurence Oliphant
books.summary: A two-volume account by the mission’s private secretary, cast as personal narrative and mostly on China, from the Canton [Guangzhou] war and Treaty of Tientsin [Tianjin] to the Yang-tse-Kiang [Yangtze] expedition, with twelve chapters on Nagasaki, Simoda [Shimoda], and Yedo [Edo] around the August 1858 treaty, more description than negotiation

books.title: A Cruise in the U.S. Steam Frigate Mississippi, Wm. C. Nicholson, Captain, to China and Japan, from July, 1857, to February, 1860
books.author: William F. Gragg
books.summary: A surgeon’s steward’s running account, without chapters, of the frigate’s 1857–1860 commission, with the storming of the Peiho [Hai River] forts, three visits to Japan at Nangasaki [Nagasaki], Simoda [Shimoda], and Hakodadi [Hakodate], nearly half the book, and the landing of Minister Harris at Jeddo [Edo] in 1859

books.title: Japan and the Japanese
books.author: “An Oriental Traveller”
books.summary: A ten-cent pamphlet for American readers, fifty-six pages compiled from the record of the American expedition, running through Japanese history from Sinmu [Jimmu] to the treaties, then government, religion, and trade, and closing on the Japanese embassy then in America

books.title: Narrative of the Earl of Elgin’s Mission to China and Japan in the Years 1857, ’58, ’59
books.author: Laurence Oliphant
books.summary: A single-volume American edition of the private secretary’s narrative of the mission, with the Canton [Guangzhou] war, the Treaty of Tientsin [Tianjin], and the Yang-tse-Kiang [Yangtze] journal, and about a quarter of it on Japan, from Nagasaki and Simoda [Shimoda] to the 1858 Treaty of Yedo [Edo]

books.title: Nagasaki and Hakodate
books.author: C. Pemberton Hodgson
books.summary: A British consul’s account of three months at Nagasaki and over a year at Hakodate in 1859–1860, with four excursions into Yezo [Hokkaido], his wife’s letters, chapters on government, priests, doctors, and houses, and an argument that Japan gained nothing by the treaties

books.title: Japan, the Amoor, and the Pacific
books.author: Henry Arthur Tilley
books.summary: An Englishman’s narrative of a circumnavigation as civilian guest in a Russian corvette in 1858–1860, with more than three months in Japan in 1859 at Nangasaki [Nagasaki], Hakodadi [Hakodate], Yedo [Edo], and Yokahama [Yokohama], then the Amoor [Amur] settlements, California, Honolulu, and Tahiti

books.title: Ten Weeks in Japan
books.author: George Smith
books.summary: The Bishop of Victoria’s record of a spring 1860 visit from China in search of missionary openings, five weeks at Nagasaki and shorter stays at Kanagawa and the British Legation at Yeddo [Edo], with blunt verdicts on Japanese and foreigners alike

vetted.result: Smith, Ten Weeks in Japan: Cornell scan cu31924023219714 (Kirtas, 300 ppi), clean; frontispiece, map (check the two overlapping leaves) and 7 woodcuts. Rule 3 not met: Ganesha / Edition Synapse 'Japan in English' (2002; CiNii BA55653925). No text at PG, OBP, Wikisource. George Smith 1815–1871. 522 images. Lower priority (reprinted).

books.title: A Lady’s Visit to Manilla and Japan
books.author: Anna D’Almeida
books.summary: A woman traveler’s narrative of an 1862 pleasure cruise from Singapore with her husband and infant daughter, three chapters on the Philippines, four on the China coast, and the later chapters on Nagasaki, Yokohama, and Kama-kura [Kamakura], with a chapter on Japanese women

vetted.result: D'Almeida, A Lady's Visit to Manilla and Japan: Cornell scan cu31924023517398 (Kirtas, 300 ppi), clean; folding frontispiece and title vignette present; the half-title leaf appears twice. Rule 3 not met: Ganesha / Edition Synapse 'Japan in English' (2003; CiNii BA65155797). No text at PG, OBP, Wikisource. First-person 1862 cruise: Hong Kong, Manila and Luzon, Macao, Shanghai, Nagasaki, Yokohama; light, chatty. Anna D'Almeida's dates unknown. 324 images. Lower priority (reprinted); readable.

books.title: The Capital of the Tycoon: A Narrative of Three Years’ Residence in Japan
books.author: Rutherford Alcock
books.summary: The British Envoy’s two-volume narrative of diplomacy at Yeddo [Edo] from June 1859 to March 1862, with the assassinations of foreigners, an audience with the Tycoon [shogun], the attack on his legation, an ascent of Fusiyama [Mt. Fuji], an overland journey from Nagasaki, and treatises on government and religion

books.title: Niphon and Pe-che-li or, Two Years in Japan and Northern China
books.author: Edward Barrington De Fonblanque
books.summary: A British officer’s narrative of 1860 in Japan buying horses for the expeditionary army in China, with Yedo [Edo], Yokuhama [Yokohama], the assassinations of foreigners, and an ascent of Fusi-jama [Mt. Fuji], followed by a garrison winter at Tien-tsin [Tianjin] and a ride to Pekin [Beijing]

books.title: Yedo and Peking: A Narrative of a Journey to the Capitals of Japan and China
books.author: Robert Fortune
books.summary: A plant collector’s narrative of two visits to Japan in 1860–1861, at Nagasaki, Kanagawa, Yedo [Edo] and its nursery gardens, and Kamakura, with conifers shipped home in Ward’s cases, a new primrose, and a closing fifth on Chefoo [Yantai], Tien-tsin [Tianjin], and Peking [Beijing]

books.title: The Treaty Ports of China and Japan. A Complete Guide to the Open Ports of Those Countries, Together with Peking, Yedo, Hongkong and Macao
books.author: N. B. Dennys, ed.
books.summary: A port-by-port guidebook for travelers and residents compiled at Hongkong [Hong Kong] with twenty-nine maps and plans, running from Hongkong, Canton [Guangzhou], and Macao [Macau] through the Chinese treaty ports to Peking [Beijing], with the last seventy pages on Nagasaki, Yokohama, Yedo [Edo], Hakodadi [Hakodate], and Hiogo [Kobe]

books.title: Greater Britain: A Record of Travel in English Speaking Countries
books.author: Charles Wentworth Dilke
books.note: Chapter on Japan originally published in “The Fortnightly Review”, October 1, 1876.
books.summary: A travel record of 1866–1867 through the English-speaking world, North America, New Zealand, Australia, and India, mixed with essays on race and empire, with a later twenty-five-page chapter, written in 1875, on the Japanese revolution and English influence

books.title: Japan, Being a Sketch of the History, Government and Officers of the Empire
books.author: Walter Dickson
books.summary: A resident’s handbook to the Japanese state, half narrative history from mythical origins to the surrender of the fiefs in 1869, half description of the court at Miako [Kyoto] and the Yedo [Edo] government, with a list of Daimios [daimyo] in 1862

books.title: Our Life in Japan
books.author: R. Mounteney Jephson and Edward Pennell Elmhirst
books.note: This book seems to be intended as semifictional humor, in the style of “Life in London” by Pierce Egan.
books.summary: A comic chronicle of garrison life at Yokohama in 1866–1867 by two English officers of the 9th Regiment, mostly hunting, pony races, and mess-night set pieces played by nicknamed messmates, with a ride to the Daiboots [Daibutsu] at Kamakura

books.title: Across America and Asia
books.author: Raphael Pumpelly
books.summary: A mining engineer’s narrative of a circuit of the globe from Arizona to Japan, where the government engaged him to explore Yesso [Hokkaido], then China and home across Mongolia and Siberia, with a chapter on Japanese art by John La Farge

books.title: China and Japan and a Voyage Thither
books.author: James B. Lawrence
books.summary: Forty-four letters to a friend from an enlisted marine on a United States naval cruise of 1865–1868, mostly China, with a tenth on Japan, Yokohama and Yeddo [Edo] in 1866 and the opening of Hiogo [Kobe] and Osaca [Osaka] in 1868

books.title: The Antipodes and Round the World, or, Travels in Australia, New Zealand, Ceylon, China, Japan, and California
books.author: Alice M. Frere
books.summary: A woman’s first-person narrative, rewritten from letters home, of a voyage round the world from Bombay [Mumbai] in 1865 with her father, through Australia, New Zealand, Ceylon [Sri Lanka], and China to Japan in 1866, Nagasaki, Yokohama, and Yedo [Edo], and home across America

books.title: Travels of a Naturalist in Japan and Manchuria
books.author: Arthur Adams
books.summary: A Royal Navy staff-surgeon’s narrative of a surveying cruise and its beetle-collecting, from Rio and the Cape through China, Korea, and Manchuria to a final third on Japan, Saghalien [Sakhalin] and its Ainos [Ainu], Hakodadi [Hakodate], Nagasaki, and the Inland Sea

books.title: Round the World: Letters from Japan, China, India, and Egypt
books.author: W. M. Perry Fogg
books.summary: Letters to a Cleveland newspaper from a sightseeing American on a westward circuit of the globe in 1870–1871, a fifth of them on a few weeks in Japan, Yokohama, Yeddo [Edo], and Nagasaki, before China, India, and Egypt

books.title: Round the World in 1870
books.author: A. D. Carlisle
books.summary: A Cambridge graduate’s journal-based narrative of a thirteen-month circuit of the globe through India, China, Japan, California, and South America, with five chapters on Japan from May 1870, Nagasaki, Osaca [Osaka], Yedo [Edo], and the Hakoni [Hakone] country under Fusi-Yama [Mt. Fuji]

books.title: New Japan, the Land of the Rising Sun
books.author: Samuel Mossman
books.summary: A compiled year-by-year chronicle of Japan from Perry’s arrival in 1853 to the reforms of 1873, drawn from earlier narratives, dispatches, and the treaty-port press, covering the treaties, the attacks on foreigners and the reprisals, and the new government of the Mikado [Emperor]

books.title: Letters Which Have Appeared in the “Japan Daily Herald”
books.author: C. J. Pfoundes
books.summary: Sixteen pseudonymous letters to a treaty-port newspaper, 1873–1874, by a foreign resident of long standing, mostly on the declining respect for foreigners in Japan, blamed on foreign residents and Japanese alike, with others on brokers, shipping, and the new government

books.title: Meeting the Sun: A Journey All Round the World
books.author: William Simpson
books.summary: A newspaper artist’s account of an eastward circuit of the globe in 1872–1873 to see the Emperor of China married, nearly half on China, with one chapter on a month in Japan, Nagasaki, the new Yokohama railway, and Kama-kura [Kamakura]

books.title: “Our Neighbourhood”; or, Sketches in the Suburbs of Yedo
books.author: Theobald A. Purcell
books.summary: Twenty-one sketches of village life in a quiet suburb of Yedo [Edo] by a foreign resident writing as one of the neighborhood, taking in the saké shop, the barber, and the blind fortune-teller, with twenty-four plates drawn in a Japanese idiom

books.title: Letters from China & Japan
books.author: Lilias Dunlop Findlay Swainson
books.summary: Forty-three letters home from a woman married at Hong-Kong [Hong Kong] to the head of the Chinese naval training department, four-fifths on the voyage out and life at the Foo-Chow [Fuzhou] arsenal, the rest a closing tour of Japan, Kobe, Yokohama, and the new railway to Yedo [Edo]

books.title: Rough Notes of Journeys Made in the Years 1868, ’69, ’70, ’71, ’72, & ’73, in Syria, Down the Tigris, India, Kashmir, Ceylon, Japan, Mongolia, Siberia, the United States, the Sandwich Islands, and Australasia
books.author: (No author indicated)
books.summary: An anonymous elderly traveler’s notes on three separate tours of 1868–1873 through Palestine, India, China, Siberia, America, and Australasia, with some sixty pages on two visits to Japan, in 1869 and in 1872–1873, the second finding Yeddo [Edo] and Osaka much changed

books.title: The Eastern Seas: Being a Narrative of the Voyage of H.M.S. "Dwarf" in China, Japan and Formosa
books.author: Bonham Ward Bax
books.summary: A naval officer’s first-person account of a gun vessel’s commission on the China station, 1871–1874, with Formosa [Taiwan], the Russian ports of Tartary, and a quarter on Japan, including an ascent of Fusi-yama [Mt. Fuji] and the Japanese expedition to Formosa of 1874

books.title: The Rambles of a Globe Trotter in Australasia, Japan, China, Java, India, and Cashmere
books.author: Egerton K. Laird
books.summary: A two-volume travel journal, in letters and dated entries, by a young man traveling on introductions through two years of wanderings, with a month in Japan in the first volume, Yokohama, Yedo [Edo], Kyoto, and the Inland Sea to Nagasaki

books.title: English Influence in Japan
books.author: Charles Wentworth Dilke
books.remark: Original publication in the Fortnightly Review of the Japan chapter of Greater Britain: A Record of Travel in English Speaking Countries (1868, above).
books.summary: A twenty-page article, an added chapter to Greater Britain after an 1875 visit, asking who made the Japanese revolution and how long English influence will last, with notes on the sale of temple bronzes and Japanese grievances against Britain

books.title: A Visit to Japan, China, and India
books.author: Robert Nicholas Fowler
books.summary: A round-the-world journal of 1875–1876 by a self-described Churchman and Tory with parliamentary interests in opium and Indian finance, giving one chapter to Japan, Yeddo [Edo], Kyoto, and Nagasaki, before the China coast and more than half the book on India

books.title: Women of the Orient: An Account of the Religious, Intellectual, and Social Condition of Women in Japan, China, India, Egypt, Syria, and Turkey
books.author: Ross C. Houghton
books.summary: A Methodist minister’s survey, arranged by topic, of women’s condition from birth and marriage to labor, widowhood, and funerals, drawn from a mission-station tour of 1873–1874, with about seventy pages on Japan and five closing chapters on women’s missionary societies

books.title: Grandmamma’s Letters from Japan
books.author: Mary Pruyn
books.summary: Twenty-nine letters of 1871–1875, mostly to her grandchildren, from a grandmother at the American Mission Home for Japanese girls at Yokohama, gathered as a children’s missionary book and mixing Japanese customs with the Home’s story and appeals for pennies

books.title: Japan: Historical and Descriptive
books.author: Charles H. Eden
books.summary: A popular survey compiled from Humbert, Lindau, and other earlier writers, with a history of Japan’s dealings with the West from Marco Polo to Perry and the murders of foreigners, and topical chapters on religion, society, daily life in Yedo [Edo], and the open ports

books.title: Life and Adventure in Japan
books.author: E. Warren Clark
books.summary: A science teacher’s first-person account of four years (1871–1875) in Japanese government service at Shidz-u-o-ka [Shizuoka] and Tokyo, written for young readers from a Christian standpoint, with the overland journey on the Tokaido and a visit to Kyoto

books.title: Child-Life in Japan
books.author: M. Chaplin Ayrton
books.summary: An illustrated book for English children on the lives of Japanese boys and girls, with seven scenes explained from plates drawn and engraved by Japanese artists, eight retold Japanese tales, and a comparison of Japanese and English games

books.title: China and Japan: A Record of Observations
books.author: I. W. Wiley
books.summary: A Methodist bishop’s record of an 1877–1878 visitation of his church’s missions in China and Japan, set against his missionary years at Foochow [Fuzhou] in the 1850s, with about a third on Japan, from Hakodate to Nagasaki, Yokohama, and Tokyo

books.title: The Sunrise Kingdom, or Life and Scenes in Japan, and Woman’s Work for Woman There
books.author: Julia D. Carrothers
books.summary: A Presbyterian missionary woman’s account of seven years in Japan, 1869–1877, from scenes of Tokyo life and the Tokaido to Hakone, through a girls’ school and its growth into a church, to closing chapters of instruction for supporters at home

books.title: Japan
books.author: Samuel Mossman
books.summary: A compact one-volume survey of Japan at the end of the 1870s, compiled from Kaempfer, Siebold, Alcock, and other authorities, in ten topical chapters on geography, history, the new army and navy, education, religion, language, arts, trade, and natural history

books.title: Japan: Its History, Traditions, and Religions, with the Narrative of a Visit in 1879
books.author: Edward J. Reed
books.summary: Two volumes by a British naval architect and Member of Parliament: a compiled history of Japan, arguing for treaty revision, and the narrative of his three-month visit of 1879 as the government’s guest, from Tokyo to Nagasaki, Osaka, Kyoto, and Ise

books.title: The Boy Travellers in the Far East: Adventures of Two Youths in a Journey to Japan and China
books.author: Thomas W. Knox
books.summary: A travel book for young readers cast as a story, following a doctor and two American youths in 1878 from Yokohama to Fusiyama [Mt. Fuji], Kyoto, and Nagasaki, then China, three-fifths of it on Japan, told by a third-person narrator with dialogue and the boys’ letters

books.title: Young Japan: Yokohama and Yedo
books.author: John R. Black
books.summary: A two-volume narrative of the Yokohama foreign settlement and of Yedo [Edo] from 1858 to 1879 by a resident newspaper editor, thick with reprinted documents, covering the assassinations, the Richardson affair, the bombardments of Kagoshima and Shimonoseki, and the revolution of 1868

books.title: Unbeaten Tracks in Japan
books.author: Isabella Bird
books.summary: Two volumes of letters by a solitary woman traveler in 1878, north from Nikkô [Nikko] to Aomori and Yezo [Hokkaido] by a route never before traversed entire by a European, with three days among the Ainos [Ainu] at Biratori, then Kiyôto [Kyoto] and Isé [Ise]

books.title: A Handbook for Travellers in Central & Northern Japan
books.author: Ernest Mason Satow
books.summary: A guidebook on the model of Murray’s Handbooks, issued at Yokohama, with fifteen sections of practical information, fifty-four numbered routes between Kōbe and Awomori [Aomori], long articles on Tōkiō [Tokyo], Kiōto [Kyoto], Nikkō, and Ise, and ascents of Fuji and other mountains

books.title: The Empire of Japan
books.author: Imperial Japanese Household Department
books.note: Prepared for Centennial Exhibition in Philadelphia in 1876
books.summary: An official pamphlet of twenty-nine pages, revised from its 1876 Centennial Exhibition edition for foreign readers, setting out the imperial line, the organization of the central government, geography and the census of 1880, an outline history, and financial, commercial, and postal statistics

books.title: Japanese Episodes
books.author: Edward Howard House
books.summary: Four first-person sketches by an American resident of Tokyo: a village romance at a mountain inn, avowedly part fiction; an ascent of Fuziyama [Mt. Fuji]; two dinners with a Japanese statesman in 1870, partly scripted as comedy; and a day in the Asakusa theater

books.title: Japan: Its Architecture, Art, and Art Manufactures
books.author: Christopher Dresser
books.summary: An architect and ornamentist’s two-part volume: a narrative of four months, received by the Mikado [Emperor] in January 1877 and then touring as guest of the nation, with sixty-eight potteries visited, followed by topical chapters on architecture, lacquer, pottery, metals, fabrics, and other manufactures

books.title: Points of Etiquette Which We Should Know and Observe in Our Social Relations with the Japanese
books.author: John C. Berry
books.summary: A missionary’s paper read to his fellow missionaries at Kobe in May 1882, largely a phrasebook of romanized Japanese, on forms of address, presents, visiting and the tea ceremony, calls of congratulation and condolence, and travel

books.title: The Land of the Morning: An Account of Japan and Its People, Based on a Four Years’ Residence in That Country, Including Travels into the Remotest Parts of the Interior
books.author: William Gray Dixon
books.summary: An Imperial College of Engineering professor’s account of four years (1876–1880) in Japan, alternating topical chapters on geography, history, Tôkiyô [Tokyo], his students, and religion with first-person journeys: a winter circuit of Fuji-san [Mt. Fuji], the Nakasendô [Nakasendo] and Tôkaidô [Tokaido] to Kiyôto [Kyoto], and the solitudes of Hida

books.title: Journal of a Lady’s Travels Round the World
books.author: F. D. Bridges
books.summary: An Englishwoman’s dated diary of some two and a half years abroad with her husband from August 1878, through Greece, Egypt, India, Kashmir, Java, and China, with five chapters on nearly four months in Japan before North America

books.title: Highways and Byeways in Japan: Experiences of Two Pedestrian Tourists
books.author: Arthur H. Crow
books.summary: A diary of four months in Japan in 1881 by a self-confessed globe-trotter walking with a friend, covering the treaty ports, a 328-mile tramp from Hikone by the Nakasendo to Takasaki and Nikko, an ascent of Fuji-san [Mt. Fuji] among pilgrims, and Hakodate in Yezo [Hokkaido]

books.summary: A returned missionary’s answers to questions asked in England, in twenty-seven short topical chapters from geography and history through babies, schools, houses, and food to religions, Christianity, and the Emperor

books.title: Japan: Country, Court, and People
books.author: J. C. Calhoun Newton
books.summary: A missionary-educator’s three-part compendium on Japan’s geography and natural history, its past from the myths through the Jesuit mission and Tokugawa seclusion, and its modern course from Perry to the 1899 treaties, ending with a forecast of Japan embracing Christianity

books.title: Japan and Its Regeneration
books.author: Otis Cary
books.summary: A mission-study textbook by a missionary in Japan, moving from the land, people, history, and religions through the Jesuit missions and the country’s reopening to modern missions, missionary methods, and present opportunities

books.title: Letters Written by the English Residents in Japan, 1611-1623
books.author: Naojiro Murakami
books.summary: A documentary collection on the English trading settlement at Hirado, reprinting William Adams’s ten letters of 1611–1617 with related petitions and privileges, a calendar of State Papers on the factory’s decade, 1613–1623, and a sixteenth-century description of Japonia [Japan]

books.title: Life in Japan, As Seen Through a Missionary’s Spectacles in the Twilight of the 19th Century
books.author: Ella Gardner
books.summary: A Cumberland Presbyterian woman missionary’s narrative and handbook from residence at Osaka, 1893–1897, written to interest the women and children of her church, with chapters on customs, festivals, and religions and a history of the mission’s stations and girls’ school

books.title: Westward to the Far East: A Guide to the Principal Cities of China and Japan with a Note on Korea
books.author: Eliza Ruhamah Scidmore
books.summary: A Canadian Pacific Railway guidebook for its own passengers, running across Canada and the Pacific to a thirty-page tour of Japan from Yokohama and Tokyo to Kyoto and Nagasaki, then a page on Korea and more on China’s treaty ports

books.title: A Handbook for Travellers in Japan
books.author: Basil Hall Chamberlain and W. B. Mason
books.summary: A sixth edition of Murray’s route-by-route guide to the whole empire from Yezo [Hokkaido] to Formosa [Taiwan], with an introduction of nearly a hundred pages on inns, costs, language, religion, and history, and eighty-five routes weighted toward Tōkyō, Nikkō, Fuji, and Kyōto

books.title: Japan: A Record in Colour
books.author: Mortimer Menpes, transcribed by Dorothy Menpes
books.summary: A color-plate album of a painter’s impressions, transcribed by his daughter in his own first person, with eleven topical chapters on the theater, the geisha, children, and craftsmen arguing that art pervades ordinary Japanese life, and 128 full-page plates
books.died_after_1955: Dorothy Menpes died in 1973 (life plus 70 years ends with 2043)

books.title: Japan: Its History, Arts, and Literature
books.author: Captain F. Brinkley
books.summary: Twelve volumes in limited editions by the editor of the Japan Mail, eight on Japan and four on China, from origins to 1867, then Tokugawa society, Meiji government, religion, festivals, commerce, art, and ceramics, correcting imperfectly informed foreign writers throughout

books.title: Japanese Plays and Playfellows
books.author: Osman Edwards
books.summary: Essays and personal reminiscences from a half-year’s stay, centered on the theater, with chapters on No [Noh] and Kiogen [Kyogen], kabuki and its actors, geisha, popular songs, an interview with Danjuro, weeks at three hot-spring resorts, and the Yoshiwara

books.title: Jinrikisha Days in Japan
books.author: Eliza Ruhamah Scidmore
books.summary: Part travel narrative and part topical survey by a repeat visitor and sometime foreign resident, from Yokohama through Tokyo to Nikko, a storm-bound ascent of Fujiyama [Mt. Fuji], Kyoto, and Nagasaki, closing in protest at the Christian nations’ bullying of Japan

books.title: Japan and Her People
books.author: Anna C. Hartshorne
books.summary: A two-volume survey grown out of three years’ residence and letters home, its chapters hung on an itinerary from Yokohama through Tokyo to Kyoto and Nagasaki but much of it history, legend, and essays on the household, the peasant, and the Ainu

scans.label: scan (volume 2)
scans.contributor: University Library, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

books.title: Japan and Its Trade
books.author: J. Morris
books.summary: A commercial handbook in Harper’s International Commerce Series, addressed to British merchants and students, with thirteen sections on population, wealth, imports and exports commodity by commodity, industry, steamship lines and ports, the tariff, currency, and the commercial outlook

books.title: Japan, Our New Ally
books.author: Alfred Stead
books.summary: A partisan survey written around the signing of the Anglo-Japanese Alliance and prefaced by Marquis Ito, arguing Japan’s fitness as a world power through trade statistics, interviews with named statesmen, reprinted documents, and a cruise with the Japanese fleet

scans.label: scan (published in the U.S. as Japan To-Day)

books.title: Sea-girt Yezo: Glimpses of Missionary Work in North Japan
books.author: John Batchelor
books.summary: A Church Missionary Society worker’s memoir of more than two decades in Yezo [Hokkaido] among Japanese and Ainu, written for young readers, with chapters on climate, pests, and blizzards, the mission’s beginnings at Hakodate, its early converts, and stories of conversion

books.title: Japanese Girls & Women
books.author: Alice Mabel Bacon
books.summary: A study of Japanese women’s lives by an American teacher at the Peeresses’ School, drawing on long friendships with Japanese ladies, moving from childhood and marriage through court, samurai, peasant, and city life to a stocktaking of ten years’ change

books.title: Around the World Via Siberia
books.author: Nicholas Senn
books.summary: A Chicago surgeon’s round-the-world narrative from newspaper letters, traveling with three medical colleagues by rail and river across Siberia to Vladivostok, then Nagasaki and Shanghai, and twenty days in Japan from the Inland Sea to Kyoto, Nikko, and Tokyo’s hospitals

scans.label: scan
scans.contributor: Francis A. Countway Library of Medicine

books.title: The Heart of Japan
books.author: Clarence Ludlow Brownell
books.summary: Thirty-seven sketches by a five-year resident lodged with a companion in two rented temples on the west coast, teaching English, taking in baths and cremations, a spendthrift samurai landlord, the first national election, Japanese views of missionaries, and duck netting

books.title: A Handbook of Modern Japan
books.author: Ernest W. Clement
books.summary: A topical compendium of condensed information on present-day Japan, in twenty-one chapters on physiography, industry, history, constitutional government, law, education, art, and religion, most closing with bibliographies, and ending in a forecast of Japan as intermediary between East and West

books.title: An Artist’s Letters from Japan
books.author: John La Farge
books.summary: A painter’s letters home from three months in 1886, covering Yokohama and Tokyo, a six-week summer at Nikko, then Kyoto and Nara, with close description of temples interleaved with essays on Taoist and Buddhist thought and Japanese art

books.title: Glimpses of Unfamiliar Japan
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.summary: Twenty-seven sketches by a teacher of English in the schools of Matsue, moving from Yokohama west to Izumo, the shrine of Kitzuki [Izumo Taisha], and the Oki islands, with a school diary and essays on the household shrine and the Japanese smile

books.title: Progress of India, Japan and China in the Century
books.author: Richard Temple
books.summary: A popular history of the century by a former Governor of Bombay, in three parts, India, Japan, and China, the short Japan part compiled from published authorities, from 1800 through Perry, the fall of the Shogunate, and the war with China to 1899

books.title: Kottō, Being Japanese Curios, with Sundry Cobwebs
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.summary: A curio-cabinet miscellany gathered by a Tokyo university lecturer, holding nine uncanny old tales retold from Japanese books, a dead Tokyo woman’s translated diary, and essays and sketches on Heiké [Heike] crabs, fireflies, a caged cricket, and the dream-eating Baku

books.title: Around the World Through Japan
books.author: Walter Del Mar
books.summary: A skeptical round-the-world narrative of 1899, more than half of it on fourteen weeks in Japan from Nagasaki through Kyoto, Shikoku, and Kyushu to Nikko, weighing the Japanese, their women, arts, and trade against the romance of earlier writers

books.title: Handbook of Japan and Japanese Exhibits at World’s Fair, St. Louis, 1904
books.author: Hajime Hoshi
books.summary: A trade handbook by a New York publisher, issued for the St. Louis fair to widen Japan’s foreign commerce, pairing nearly a hundred pages of statistics on government, population, industries, trade, and Formosa [Taiwan] with a building-by-building tour of the Japanese exhibits

books.title: Impressions of Japan
books.author: George H. Rittner
books.summary: A traveler’s record arranged by theme in eleven chapters on natural beauties, the arts, bathing, children, the geisha, the stage, and temples, with polemical chapters blaming the treaties for corrupting Japanese art and morals and attacking the missionaries

books.title: Japan: An Attempt at Interpretation
books.author: Lafcadio Hearn
books.summary: A fourteen-year resident’s sociological essay on Japanese national character, tracing family, state, samurai loyalty, and Tokugawa discipline back to ancestor-worship in its domestic, communal, and national forms, with constant reference to Herbert Spencer, closing on the war with Russia

books.title: Japan: The Place and the People
books.author: G. Waldo Browne
books.summary: A pictorial account in forty-one chapters, introduced by the Japanese Minister to the United States, touring Yokohama, Tokyo, and Kyoto before ten chapters of history, the Restoration, and the war with China, with over three hundred colored plates and half-tones

books.title: Japan and the Japanese As Seen by Foreigners Prior to the Beginning of the Russo-Japanese War
books.author: Karl Kiyoshi Kawakami (editor)
books.summary: An anthology of excerpts from foreign, mostly American and British, writers on Japanese character, women, art, and manners, compiled in Seattle for young Japanese readers, with an introduction setting such praise against the treatment of Japanese on the Pacific coast

books.title: Japan: Aspects and Destinies
books.author: W. Petrie Watson
books.summary: A three-year resident and newspaper leader-writer’s polemical treatise, issued on the eve of war with Russia, with a hundred pages on manners as prologue to arguments on Osaka’s mill girls, a still-born constitution, ancestor-worship, and Japan’s place on the Pacific rim

books.title: Japan in Pictures
books.author: Douglas Sladen
books.summary: A topically arranged picture-book of nearly seventy full-page photographic plates, its six chapters on water life, crops and flowers, landscapes, temples, street life, and how the Japanese live each opened by several pages of prose

books.title: Japan in the Beginning of the Twentieth Century
books.author: Department of Agriculture and Commerce
books.summary: An official survey of Japan’s economic life compiled for the Louisiana Purchase Exposition, 828 pages of text and statistical tables on geography, agriculture, industry, trade, finance, the army and navy, communications, and education, with a supplement on Formosa [Taiwan]

books.title: Japan To-Day
books.author: James A. B. Scherer
books.summary: A kaleidoscopic account of five years mostly spent teaching English at a government school in Saga, with chapters on home life, religion, and the Ainu, a life of the missionary Verbeck, and a wartime brief for Japan’s cause against Russia

books.title: Present-Day Japan
books.author: Augusta M. Campbell Davidson
books.summary: A woman traveler’s letters home from an extended stay made without guides, rearranged by place and subject into chapters on Yokohama, inland travel and country inns, Shinto and Buddhism, Kyoto, Nikko, and above all Tokyo, closing with the theater

books.title: Queer Things About Japan
books.author: Douglas Sladen
books.summary: An Englishman’s comic memoir of Japanese street life and domestic manners, drawn from months of housekeeping in Tokyo and Yokohama, with chapters on houses, women, servants, shopping, festivals, geisha, and the theater, and a closing itinerary from Yokohama to Nagasaki

books.title: To the Golden East: Being a Résumé of the Author’s Experiences in India, China, Japan, &c.
books.author: Hubert Holliday
books.summary: A diary-like travelogue of six months in 1902 as a saloon passenger on a tramp steamer from London to Shanghai, Japan, Java, and Calcutta [Kolkata], some six of its forty-two chapters covering Nagasaki, Moji, and Shimonoseki and the largest share India

books.title: Wonders of Japan: A Portfolio of Views in the Enchanted Bamboo-land
books.author: (No author listed)
books.summary: A New York souvenir album of some fifty full-page captioned photographs, prefaced by a short essay on Japan’s rise and the war with Russia, picturing Nikko shrines, Kyoto temples, street trades, tea-picking, marriage customs, Fujiyama [Mt. Fuji], Miyajima, and a wartime Nagasaki

books.title: The New Far East
books.author: Arthur Diósy
books.summary: A political argument by the chairman of council of the Japan Society, written in 1898 and reissued at the outbreak of the war with Russia, comparing Japan, China, and Korea in character, women, commerce, and fighting power, and urging an Anglo-Japanese alliance

books.title: Two Years in Three Continents: Experiences, Impressions and Observations of Two Americans Abroad
books.author: Edgar M. Condit
books.summary: A retired businessman’s letters to his Iowa home paper from a two-year tour through Europe, Egypt, the Holy Land, Siberia, China, and India, with six chapters on two and a half months in Japan in 1903 and an eye for missions and schools

books.title: Letters from Japan
books.author: Mrs. Hugh Fraser
books.summary: Letters from the British Minister’s wife during three years’ residence in Tokyo from 1889, on court audiences, treaty revision and the bombing of Count Okuma, the first Diet, the Otsu attack on the Cesarévitch [Tsarevich], festivals and legends, and Catholic missions

books.title: An American Cruiser in the East
books.author: John D. Ford
books.summary: A U.S. naval officer’s narrative of a three-year cruise, ordered in 1890, through the Aleutians and Behring Sea [Bering Sea] to Japan, Korea, China, Formosa [Taiwan], and the Philippines, nearly a third of it on Japan, from Yokohama and Tokyo to Kobe and Nagasaki

books.title: From Egypt to Japan
books.author: Henry M. Field
books.summary: The second half of a clergyman’s round-the-world journey, from Constantinople [Istanbul] in 1875 through Egypt, India, Java, and China, with theology and missions weighed at almost every stop, reaching Japan only in a final chapter on Yokohama, Yedo [Edo], and the Tokaido

books.title: Imperial Japan: The Country and Its People
books.author: George William Knox
books.summary: A systematic survey by a former missionary of fifteen years’ residence, from the Ko-Ji-Ki [Kojiki] through feudal war and the nineteenth-century opening to Buddhism, Confucianism, the samurai’s code and life, women, and education, with translated sermons and Arai Hakuseki’s autobiography

books.title: Japan: From the Old to the New
books.author: Robert Grant Webster
books.summary: A barrister and former M.P.’s account, quoting at length his letters from a residence in 1870, running from first impressions of Nagasaki through feudal history, Bushido, and women’s status to the wars with China and Russia and the Anglo-Japanese alliance

books.title: Japan As Seen and Described by Famous Writers
books.author: Esther Singleton (editor and translator)
books.summary: An anthology of forty-six excerpts from some thirty writers, among them Chamberlain, Hearn, Loti, Edwin Arnold, and Isabella Bird Bishop, arranged in six parts on the country, history and religion, places, manners and customs, arts and crafts, and modern Japan

books.title: Japan, the Eastern Wonderland
books.author: D. C. Angus
books.summary: A Japanese man’s life story, framed as letters to a London professor’s young daughter, from a rice farm and a Yedo [Edo] swordsmith’s forge through court life in Kyoto and the wars ending the Shogunate to the reforms of the 1870s

books.title: More Queer Things About Japan
books.author: Douglas Sladen and Norma Lorimer
books.summary: A miscellany reissued as a Peace Edition after the war with Russia, comprising Norma Lorimer’s essays on Japan from a woman’s point of view, a Japanese life of Napoleon, Will Adams’s letters, Douglas Sladen’s chapters from a man’s, and an appendix on the Yoshiwara

books.title: My Travels in China, Japan, and Java, 1903
books.author: The Raja-I Rajgan Jagatjit Singh of Kapurthala
books.summary: An Indian raja’s record of a journey in 1903 by Ceylon [Sri Lanka], China, and Port Arthur [Lüshun] to Japan and Dutch Java, its longest chapter on legation parties, army maneuvers, and an audience with the Emperor, with comparisons to India throughout

books.title: Religion in Japan: Shintoism, Buddhism, Christianity
books.author: George A. Cobbold
books.summary: A doctrinal survey issued by the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, written in 1893 after a visit though not published until 1905, with chapters on Shinto, Buddhism and its Japanese sects, parallels with Roman Catholic ceremonial, and the Christian missions

books.title: The Japan-Russia War: An Illustrated History of the War in the Far East, the Greatest Conflict of Modern Times
books.author: Sydney Tyler
books.summary: A war correspondent’s illustrated history for American readers, in twenty chapters from the diplomatic quarrel over Manchuria and Korea through Port Arthur [Lüshun], the Yalu, Liaoyang, Mukden [Shenyang], and Tsushima to the Portsmouth treaty, reprinted in full, with photographs and campaign maps

books.title: Young Japan: The Story of the Japanese People and Especially of Their Educational Development
books.author: James A. B. Scherer
books.summary: A popular history from mythological beginnings to the war with Russia by a former government-school teacher, cast as a nation’s childhood, adolescence, and school-days, pairing political history with educational development, down to a closing argument over moral instruction

books.title: A Woman Alone in the Heart of Japan
books.author: Gertrude Adams Fisher
books.summary: An American woman tourist’s narrative of a season traveling largely alone by third-class rail and riksha, from Yokohama to Kyoto, six weeks at Nikko, and the Kusatsu sulfur baths, turning in its last five chapters to schools and women’s education

books.title: A Guide-Book for Tourists in Japan
books.author: The Welcome Society
books.summary: A travel manual in its second, revised edition, compiled by a Tokyo society for welcoming foreign visitors, with sample itineraries, tables of fares and charges, numbered routes from Yokohama, Kobe, and Nagasaki, extensions to Formosa [Taiwan] and Korea, and a phrasebook

books.title: An English Girl in Japan
books.author: Ella M. Hart Bennett
books.summary: A memoir drawn from the diary of an Englishwoman arriving at eighteen with her widowed father, on an extended residence in Tokyo with court occasions, chapters on ladies, children, servants, and her chow dog, and a last chapter in Assam

books.title: Great Japan: A Study of National Efficiency
books.author: Alfred Stead
books.summary: A work of advocacy holding up Japanese national efficiency as an object-lesson to British readers, with a foreword by Rosebery, in twenty chapters on the throne, patriotism, Bushido, education, industry, humane warfare, women, and Formosa [Taiwan], built largely from quoted documents

books.title: The Garter Mission to Japan
books.author: Lord Redesdale
books.summary: Journal letters home by a member of the 1906 mission that invested the Emperor with the Order of the Garter, covering the investiture in Tokyo, naval arsenals, Kyoto, and Kagoshima, with memories of his own service in Japan from 1866

books.title: Japan
books.author: David Murray
books.summary: A narrative history in the Story of the Nations series by a former superintendent of education in Japan (1873–1879), running from the creation myths to the war with Russia, its final chapters completed by another hand after his death

books.title: Makers of Japan
books.author: J. Morris
books.summary: A collective biography written from London by a partisan of the Anglo-Japanese alliance, portraying the Emperor, the last Shogun, three martyred reformers, and the statesmen, soldiers, and financiers of the new Japan, from Ito and Saigo to Togo and Shibusawa

books.title: The Land of the Tatami: Travels in Japan
books.author: George T. Murray
books.summary: Wry travel sketches by a Shanghai-based writer, reprinted from his newspaper columns, recounting a loop through wartime Japan in 1904–1905, from Kobe and Kyoto to Tokyo and Kyushu, with two months among convalescing soldiers at the hot springs of Arima

books.title: Vacation Days in Hawaii and Japan
books.author: Charles M. Taylor
books.summary: A tourist’s day-by-day journal of an extended holiday from Philadelphia, with several chapters on the Hawaiian Islands and two-thirds of the book on Japan: Yokohama, Nikko, a flood-stalled inland circuit through Nagano and Sendai, the Tokaido, Kyoto, and Nara

books.title: Life of Japan
books.author: Masuji Miyakawa
books.summary: A Japanese writer’s three-part exposition of his country for American readers, covering national character and relations with the United States from Perry through the wars with China and Russia, and closing with ten reasons why an American-Japanese war is impossible

books.title: Old and New Japan
books.author: Clive Holland
books.summary: A topical survey of Japanese civilization rather than a record of travel, running from the creation myths through religion, home life, festivals, language, gardens, and folklore to the treaty ports, with fifty full-page color plates by Montagu Smyth

books.title: Our Journey to Japan
books.author: Jacob Schiff
books.summary: A privately printed keepsake of a spring 1906 visit by the underwriter of Japan’s war loans and his wife, recording an audience and private luncheon with the Emperor, dinners from the Finance Minister and bankers, and a side trip to Seoul

books.title: Shinto: The Ancient Religion of Japan
books.author: W. G. Aston
books.summary: A short expository treatise in the series Religions Ancient and Modern, surveying Shinto’s sources, myths, gods, priesthood, worship, purity, and divination, and closing with the judgment that Shinto, lacking a moral code, an ecclesiastical organization, or a developed sacred literature, is doomed to extinction

books.title: The Future of Japan, with a Survey of Present Conditions
books.author: W. Petrie Watson
books.summary: A work of philosophical argument rather than travel, by a writer with some years’ residence in Japan, surveying present conditions from the constitution to morals, then asking whether Japan can offer Europe any new religion or idea, and answering no

books.title: Wanderings East of Suez, in Ceylon, India, China and Japan
books.author: Frederic Courtland Penfield
books.summary: A travel narrative through Ceylon [Sri Lanka], India, and the China coast, framed by an argument about American trade, with Japan confined to a final chapter, an essay written just after the war with Russia on its debt, shipbuilding, and commercial prospects

books.title: In Togo’s Country: Some Studies in Satsuma and Other Little Known Parts of Japan
books.author: Henry R. Schwartz
books.summary: Essays from fourteen years’ residence in out-of-the-way parts of Japan, centered on a study of the history and customs of Satsuma, home province of Togo, Oyama, and Kuroki, with chapters on Loo Choo [Ryukyu], Shimoda, Nagasaki, and the war with Russia

books.title: Summer Greetings from Japan
books.author: Walter L. Sheldon
books.summary: Sixteen privately printed letters home from summer 1906 by a visitor from the St. Louis Ethical Society, introduced in Tokyo to university professors, Count Okuma, and the Prime Minister, giving three public lectures, and touring Kyoto, Sendai, and flood-struck Nikko
books.died_after_1955: Anna Cope Hartshorne, who wrote the two-page introductory letter, died in 1957 (life plus 70 years ends with 2027)

books.title: The Far East Revisited; Essays on Political, Commercial, Social, and General Conditions in Malaya, China, Korea and Japan
books.author: A. Gorton Angier
books.summary: A journalist’s letters from a return tour through Malaya [Malaysia], China, and Korea, with a preface by Sir Robert Hart, ending in four chapters on Japan’s postwar finance, dockyards and factories, Tokyo, and the coal and iron of Hokkaido and Kamaishi

books.title: The Social Evil in Japan and Allied Subjects: With Statistics, Social Evil Test Cases, and Progress of the Antibrothel Movement
books.author: U. G. Murphy
books.summary: A Nagoya Methodist missionary’s exposé of Japan’s licensed-prostitution system, setting out its mechanics with statistics, then narrating in the first person his test lawsuits from 1899 on behalf of women seeking to leave the brothels, with translated court judgments appended

books.title: Japanese Life in Town and Country
books.author: George William Knox
books.summary: A topical account by a missionary of fifteen years’ residence, moving from history through Buddhism, Confucianism, and the samurai ethic, illustrated by his own translations, to a first-person stay among the samurai of Tosa and chapters on farmers, merchants, and women

books.title: The Newest Way Round the World
books.author: Celeste J. Miller
books.summary: A woman’s first-person narrative of a ten-month circumnavigation from Chicago in 1902 by way of the new Trans-Siberian Railway, Korea, China, Siam [Thailand], and Java, with five admiring chapters on Japan, from Nagasaki and Kyoto to the Ise shrines and Tokyo

books.title: Every-day Japan: Written After Twenty-Five Years’ Residence and Work in the Country
books.author: Arthur Lloyd
books.summary: A subject-by-subject survey of late-Meiji Japan in sixty-four chapters by a British clergyman and lecturer at Tokyo’s Imperial University and naval and commercial colleges, from the throne, the Diet, and the courts to village life, trades, schools, and the Yoshiwara

books.title: The Arts of Japan
books.author: Edward Dillon
books.summary: A compact survey in Methuen’s Little Books on Art series, compiled from published scholarship and recollections of a former residence in Japan, tracing painting and sculpture from the dolmen tombs to Hokusai, then prints, sword furniture, netsuke, lacquer, and ceramics

books.title: The Empire of the East, A Simple Account of Japan as It Was, Is, and Will Be
books.author: H. B. Montgomery
books.summary: A popular, topically arranged survey by a lay observer just back from another visit to Japan, covering religion, the constitution, daily life, trade, the arts, and morality before two chapters of forecast, with one first-person visit to Kyoto’s Buddhist temples

books.title: Behind the Screens: An English Woman’s Impressions of Japan
books.author: Evelyn Adam
books.summary: Fourteen self-contained essays, without itinerary or illustrations, recording six years’ observation of Japanese life from inside the house rather than the street: marriage, mimicry, red tape, present-giving, excuses, and a Young Japan spoiled by praise after the war with Russia

books.title: A Journal from Japan
books.author: Marie C. Stopes
books.summary: A woman scientist’s diary of eighteen months (1907–1909) hunting coal-mine fossils from Hokkaido to Kiushiu [Kyushu] and working with Japanese scientists at the university, by her own account the first Western woman scientist to do so, and lamenting the brick and smoke spoiling Japan’s beauty
books.died_after_1955: Marie Stopes died in 1958 (life plus 70 years ends with 2028)

books.title: Rare Days in Japan
books.author: George Trumbull Ladd
books.summary: A memoir of twelve excursions and occasions from three visits (1892, 1899, and 1906–1907) by a lecturer several times received by the Emperor, from the Imperial Diet, the Katsura rapids, and Asama-yama [Mt. Asama] to No [Noh] drama, Nichiren’s Ikegami, and the court

books.title: A Journal of the Perry Expedition to Japan (1853–1854)
books.author: S. Wells Williams
books.summary: The day-by-day diary of the expedition’s first interpreter, a Canton [Guangzhou] missionary-printer and sinologist, running from April 1853 to August 1854 through Lewchew [Ryukyu], the landing at Kurihama, the Treaty of Kanagawa, and weeks ashore at Simoda [Shimoda] and Hakodade [Hakodate]

books.title: Highways and Homes of Japan
books.author: Kate Lawson
books.summary: A woman traveler’s narrative of two long visits, after a posting as a correspondent in India, opening at Nagasaki, Kyōto, and Tōkyō and widening into topical chapters on the arts, festivals, women, and Meiji statesmen, with plates from her own Kodak

books.title: Historical and Geographical Dictionary of Japan
books.author: E. Papinot
books.summary: A two-volume alphabetical reference work on Japanese history and geography, with entries on persons, places, offices, customs, and sects from mythology to the Meiji era, a supplement on Westerners in Japan 1542–1868, and eighteen appendixes, compiled from a Catholic standpoint

books.title: In Lotus-Land Japan
books.author: Herbert G. Ponting
books.summary: A photographer’s account of three years of travel in Japan between 1903 and 1906, arranged by place and topic, from Kyoto’s temples and craftsmen to volcanoes, Fuji, Tokyo’s flower festivals, and the Ainu of Yezo [Hokkaido], with over a hundred plates

books.title: Japan & the Japanese
books.author: Walter Tyndale
books.summary: An English watercolor painter’s chronicle of roughly a year in Japan, from Moji in May to the following February, with stays at Kyoto, the Fuji lakes, Nikko, Tokyo, and Atami, and thirty-two color plates of his own paintings

books.title: Japan To-Day: A Souvenir of the Anglo-Japanese Exhibition Held in London 1910
books.author: Kotaro Mochizuki
books.summary: A 772-page souvenir volume for the Anglo-Japanese Exhibition by a Tokyo news-agency president, with portraits of sovereigns, autographs and commendations from ambassadors and statesmen, a historical outline, a railway-line guide to scenery, a survey of government, and several hundred profiles of firms and businessmen

books.title: A Vagabond Journey Around the World
books.author: Harry A. Franck
books.summary: A first-person narrative of a moneyless working journey around the globe begun in 1904, through Europe, Egypt, India, and Siam [Thailand] to China, with some thirty pages on a tramp from Nagasaki to Yokohama shadowed by police spies during the war with Russia
books.died_after_1955: Harry A. Franck died in 1962 (life plus 70 years ends with 2032)

books.title: Picturesque Japan
books.author: Chester R. Stratton
books.summary: A compiled survey of Japanese history, religion, and customs, from the legendary founding of the empire to the war with China of 1894–1895, drawn largely from other writers, above all the Swiss minister Aimé Humbert’s first-person account of Yokohama and Tokyo

books.title: Sights and Scenes in Fair Japan
books.author: Imperial Government Railways
books.summary: An oblong picture album of forty-eight mostly hand-colored photographs captioned in English for visitors, with no other text, running from Tokyo through Kamakura, Fuji, Kyōto, Nara, and the Inland Sea to Kyūshū, Nikko, and Matsushima, bound in woven textile covers

books.title: The Shinto Cult: A Christian Study of the Ancient Religion of Japan
books.author: Milton Spenser Terry
books.summary: A short manual condensed from a comparative-religion teacher’s lectures on ancient Shinto, drawn from published scholarship rather than firsthand encounter, covering its sources, mythology, shrines, rituals, and fusion with Buddhism, with a closing Christian assessment of its defects and possible fulfillment

books.title: The Story of Old Japan
books.author: Joseph H. Longford
books.summary: A popular history of Japan from the creation myths to the fall of the shogunate, by a former British consul at Nagasaki with thirty-three years’ residence, covering the Taira and Minamoto wars, the Mongol invasions, and the Christian missions and their persecution

books.title: Winter Wanderings; Being an Account of Travels in Abyssinia, Samoa, Java, Japan, the Philippines, Australia, South America and Other Interesting Countries
books.author: Abraham Per Lee Pease
books.summary: An Ohio physician’s travel letters, mostly newspaper dispatches, from four winter journeys, to Abyssinia [Ethiopia] with an American diplomatic commission, around the world, through the Pacific islands and Australia, and to South America, with four chapters on Japan in November 1904 during the war with Russia

books.title: An Army Officer on Leave in Japan
books.author: L. Mervin Maus
books.summary: A narrative of a journey to Japan with two lecturing companions, the Major and the Judge, giving its first quarter to Manila and Formosa [Taiwan] before Nagasaki, Tokyo, Nikko, Kyoto, and Miyajima, with chapters on mythology, history, religion, and the Russo-Japanese War

books.title: From Japan to Jerusalem
books.author: E. Graham Ingham
books.summary: A bishop’s dated diary of an eight-month round-the-world inspection of Church Missionary Society stations in 1909–1910, giving its opening fifth to Japan, from Osaka and Kyoto to Hokkaido, a Tokyo missions conference, and Kiu-Shiu [Kyushu], before China, Ceylon [Sri Lanka], India, Palestine, and Egypt

books.title: Japan for a Week (Britain For Ever)
books.author: A. M. Thompson
books.summary: A comic, opinionated narrative of a dash through Russia and Siberia to Japan seeking local color for a play, with two-fifths of the book there, chiefly Kyoto, Tokyo, and Nikko, then China, and closing essays on the German menace and imperial patriotism

books.title: Surface Japan: Short Notes of a Swift Survey
books.author: Don Carlos Seitz
books.summary: A run of short undated notes and anecdotes by a visiting outsider guided by Japanese friends, from Yokohama and Tokyo to Nikko, Hakone, and the Inland Sea, with a middle argument on Japan’s taxation, war debt, new dependencies, and the color line

books.title: The Far East, China, Korea, & Japan
books.author: Frank Elias
books.summary: A topical survey of eastern Asia written for young readers and compiled from other travelers’ books, giving nineteen of its forty-four chapters to Japan, from Xavier and Will Adams to women, children, schooling, flower arrangement, and trades, with thirty-two color plates

books.title: Things Seen in Japan
books.author: Clive Holland
books.summary: An illustrated guide to Japanese life in six topical chapters, written in an impersonal register with no account of the author’s own travels, covering flowers and gardens, etiquette, home life and the duties of women, crafts, Shinto and Buddhism, and festivals

books.title: Where Half the World Is Waking Up: The Old and the New in Japan, China, the Philippines, and India
books.author: Clarence Hamilton Poe
books.summary: Dispatches from a year-long tour of Asia by the editor of a North Carolina farm paper, giving six of twenty-six chapters to Japan, especially its farming and factories, then Korea, Manchuria, China, the Philippines, and India, with special reference to American conditions
books.died_after_1955: Clarence Poe died in 1964 (life plus 70 years ends with 2034)

books.title: Fourteen Years of Diplomatic Life in Japan
books.author: Baroness Albert d’Anethan
books.summary: An Englishwoman’s day-by-day diary as wife of the Belgian Minister at Tokyo from October 1893 to March 1906, recording court audiences, legation society, the war with China, the Boxer crisis, and the war with Russia as seen from the capital

books.title: A Gentle Jehu in Japan
books.author: Ethel L. McLean
books.summary: A private-press diary in dated entries by one of two women traveling together, from a transcontinental train journey and a Pacific crossing via Honolulu to a spring in Japan, with Kyoto’s Cherry Dance, Miyajima, Nara, Tokyo at Easter, and Kamakura

books.title: Japan and Japanese-American Relations
books.author: George H. Blakeslee (editor)
books.summary: Twenty-two addresses from a Clark University conference on Japan by American and Japanese speakers including David Starr Jordan and Inazo Nitobe, collected to counter postwar suspicion between the two countries, on immigration, national character, industry, trade, missions, diplomacy, and colonial administration

books.title: Japan As I Saw It
books.author: A. H. Exner
books.summary: A traveler’s book opening with a sixty-nine-page history of Japan from the gods to the death of Mutsu Hito [Mutsuhito], then a journey from Nagasaki eastward through Kyoto, Yokohama, Tokyo, and Nikko, mixed with topical surveys of customs and religion

books.title: Japan of the Japanese
books.author: Joseph H. Longford
books.summary: A sixteen-chapter survey of Japan by a King’s College professor of Japanese and former consul at Nagasaki with thirty years’ residence, covering national character, history, the Imperial family and samurai, women, language and literature, law, the armed forces, railways, and trade
